title: Scheduler metrics: prefill/decode split, queue depth histograms, and backpressure counters
author: Julian Moore
body:
Context: For the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we keep seeing cases where microbench wins don’t show up end-to-end. The primary missing piece has been scheduler-level visibility into (a) how much wall time is spent in prefill vs decode, (b) how deep the internal queues get under mixed workloads, and (c) when we’re applying backpressure (and why). This PR adds low-overhead instrumentation to make benchmark runs interpretable and to support perf-canary gating by workload regime.

What’s in this PR: 1) Prefill/decode split metrics: We now record scheduler-attributed time and token counters separately for prefill and decode paths. This is emitted both as per-request spans (when tracing is enabled) and as runtime histograms/counters (always on). New metrics: runtime.scheduler.prefill.duration_ms (histogram), runtime.scheduler.decode.duration_ms (histogram), runtime.scheduler.prefill.tokens (counter), runtime.scheduler.decode.tokens (counter), runtime.scheduler.prefill.batch_size (histogram), runtime.scheduler.decode.batch_size (histogram). 2) Queue depth histograms: Adds queue-depth tracking for the admission queue and per-stage work queues. Metric names: runtime.scheduler.queue_depth{queue=admission|prefill|decode} (histogram) and runtime.scheduler.queue_wait_ms{queue=admission|prefill|decode} (histogram). 3) Backpressure counters: Adds explicit counters for each throttle mechanism, tagged with reason. Metric: runtime.scheduler.backpressure_total{reason=max_inflight|max_kv_mem|max_batch_window|gpu_oom_guard|prefill_starvation_guard}. 4) Tagging for benchmark interpretability: All above metrics include tags for model, gpu_sku, and kernel_mode when present in the request context (this is wired through the existing RequestContext; no new global labels). 5) Minimal overhead + sampling: Queue depth sampling happens on enqueue/dequeue transitions and is aggregated per worker loop tick; per-request tracing is gated behind existing tracing config.

Why this helps: The benchmark suite mixes prompt-length distributions and concurrency. Without a prefill/decode split, a kernel change that improves decode but increases prefill launch overhead can look like a regression depending on traffic mix. Queue depth histograms tell us whether we’re actually compute-bound or scheduler/backpressure-bound. Backpressure reasons are required for anomaly triage (e.g., KV memory guard vs batching window).

Implementation notes: - Prefill vs decode attribution is done at the scheduler boundary (right before dispatch to the engine) rather than inside kernels. This keeps it stable across kernel variants. - Queue depth is measured as observed length at enqueue and before dispatch; we record both depth and wait time to disambiguate bursty vs sustained pressure. - Backpressure counters are incremented at the exact decision point where a request is delayed/rejected from immediate scheduling, including a single canonical reason (priority order documented in code).

Rollout/compatibility: - Metrics are additive; no existing names changed. - Cardinality: model/gpu_sku/kernel_mode already exist in other runtime metrics; this PR does not introduce new high-cardinality fields like request_id. - Export is through the standard stats pipeline; no dashboard changes included here (tracked in ENG-7427).

Test plan: - unit: scheduler_metrics_test covers attribution (prefill vs decode), queue depth/wait time recording, and backpressure reason selection. - integration: ran local loadgen (mixed prefill/decode) and verified metrics emission in /metrics and tracing span annotations. - benchmark: executed a small calibration run from the harness to confirm metrics align with known workload parameters.

Follow-ups: - Grafana panels + canary thresholds will be updated in ENG-7427/ENG-7426. - Once kernel_mode tagging PR lands broadly, we can slice prefill/decode splits by kernel mode without additional changes.

Screenshots/outputs: Included in the internal comment thread are sample Prometheus outputs for queue_depth and backpressure_total during a bursty 64-concurrency run (H100), showing decode queue saturation and max_kv_mem backpressure during long-context prompts.
commits: metrics: add queue depth + queue wait histograms
metrics: add backpressure counters with canonical reason selection
tracing: annotate spans with scheduler stage + queue wait
tests: scheduler metrics attribution and backpressure reason tests
review_thread: Sofia Ivanova (request changes): Can we ensure prefill/decode attribution is scheduler-boundary only? I don’t want kernel variants to change accounting. Also concerned about the backpressure reason priority order being implicit. Julian Moore (reply): Attribution is only at the scheduler boundary (before engine dispatch). I added a comment + a small helper enum to keep it explicit. I also documented reason priority in scheduler.h and added a unit test asserting the priority when multiple guards would apply. Omar El-Sayed (comment): Queue depth histogram buckets—can we avoid linear buckets that will blow up memory? We mostly care about 0-256 range but want visibility for extreme outliers. Julian Moore (reply): Switched to exponential buckets (1,2,4,...,2048) with a clamp at 4096, and added an explicit ‘overflow’ bucket via histogram max. Marcus Reed (comment): The queue_wait_ms recording should start at enqueue timestamp, but make sure we don’t call steady_clock too often in the hot path. Julian Moore (reply): Used a cached tick per worker loop iteration; enqueue stores a uint64 monotonic timestamp already present for other scheduling logic. Added a micro-benchmark in tests to ensure we don’t regress by more than 1–2%. Allison Grant (approve): Tagging looks consistent with other runtime metrics; thanks for avoiding request_id. Please coordinate with ENG-7427 for dashboard slices. Sofia Ivanova (approve): Looks good after the priority-order test + bucket update. Merge when CI is green.
